Seat note for phase 3 · 2026-11-08T05:09Z · ⛔ Not a claim.

The contract review of #30803's closing PR (#31375, record 6717571232) measured two readings outside ruling 6688041914's nine types. Phase 3's design should know about both:

- **`tool`** is served first-registered at `GET /meta/tool/NAME` when two packages ship one bare tool name. A third package installed after the boot answers 200 and is shadowed. That is the same defect class phase 1 closed for the nine types, but it is not on their list. Phase 3's namespaced names resolve it; until then it is open. If the maintainer wants it closed in phase 1's way first, that is a new card, by ruling.
- **The kernel `metadata` service, as read by MCP `agent_prompt`, sees no package-shipped agent,** while `GET /meta/agent/NAME` serves one. The two readers of "an agent by name" disagree (ADR-0063 §2 direction). Name the one reader when phase 3 rewrites agent resolution.

## Phase 3 migration plan (design) — for seat review

Card #30806, step 1 (design only: no branch, no PR, no repo file changed). Ruling C on #30798 (「同意 c」). Measured on objectstack `origin/main` `1ff99441` and hotcrm `origin/main` `6961ab1`, read 2026-11-08T09:29Z. Placeholders below are spelled `NS`, `SHORT`, `NAME` (the GitHub sanitizer eats angle-bracket shapes).

**One-paragraph summary.** The objectstack tree has nothing left to rename: every namespaced example, the template and the three connector apps measure 0 bare names. All of the first-party work is hotcrm: 206 items (187 distinct names) in 4 of its 5 packages. The hard part is live data. A rename silently detaches stored by-name references; 17 of the 21 kinds in §2 need a rewrite: permission-set and position assignments, activation switches, overlays and environment bodies, paused runs, hook secrets, OAuth connections, and others. So the order that keeps live environments safe is: spec rule, then save door, then the stored-reference migration, then ADRs, then the hotcrm renames, which ship only on a release that carries the migration. Third parties: refuse loudly from the release that ships the rule, plus an executable migration-chain entry. There is no warning window and no load-time conversion, unless the maintainer names an external package that needs one. Five questions need a maintainer answer; they are at the end.

### 1. First-party size (re-measured)

Method: `os lint --json` from the tree's own CLI (built at `1ff99441`), rule `naming/namespace-prefix`, counting findings that carry a `fix` (a bare name; the duplicate finding has none). Raw outputs are under the dev's scratchpad; the commands are re-runnable as written.

| Package | Namespace | Bare names | By type |
|:--|:--|--:|:--|
| examples/app-todo | todo | 0 | (phase 2 baseline 20 → 0, PR #30927) |
| examples/app-crm | crm | 0 | (7 → 0; `guest_portal` exempt by ruling 6687835712) |
| examples/app-showcase | showcase | 0 | (12 → 0) |
| examples/app-multi-package | crm | 0 | (1 → 0) |
| examples/embed-objectql | none | n/a | no `objectstack.config.ts`, no manifest namespace |
| create-objectstack `blank` template | blank | 0 | by inspection, as in phase 2 (`blank_note` only; the template has no install to load, `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`) |
| packages/apps/connector-stripe, -docusign, -github | stripe, docusign, github | 0 each | |
| packages/services/service-i18n config | n/a | 0 | |
| **hotcrm** `app.objectstack.hotcrm.service` | crm | **34** | actions 8, hooks 8, flows 6, reports 3, sharingRules 3, pages 1, dashboards 1, datasets 1, queues 1, assignmentRules 1, skills 1 |
| **hotcrm** `app.objectstack.hotcrm.revenue` | crm | **33** | hooks 19, actions 7, flows 4, pages 2, datasets 1 |
| **hotcrm** `app.objectstack.hotcrm.marketing` | crm | **14** | hooks 6, flows 4, actions 2, sharingRules 2 |
| **hotcrm** `app.objectstack.hotcrm.o2c` | crm | 0 | |
| **hotcrm** `app.objectstack.hotcrm` (the App) | crm | **125** | actions 23, hooks 22, flows 21, positions 12, pages 7, reports 7, datasets 7, sharingRules 6, permissions 5, skills 5, picklists 5, dashboards 3, queues 1, assignmentRules 1 |

- hotcrm total: **206 items, 187 distinct names**. By type: hooks 55, actions 40, flows 35, sharingRules 11, pages 10, reports 10, datasets 9, positions 12, skills 6, permissions 5, picklists 5, dashboards 4, queues 2, assignmentRules 2. The longest rename is `crm_knowledge_article_publish_timestamps` (40 characters).
- Reference churn in hotcrm, as an upper bound: the 187 names appear quoted 2,952 times across 493 files in `src/`, `test/`, `e2e/`, `docs/` and `content/` (`git grep -c` per name). Short words such as `industry` (a picklist) also match field names, so the real count is lower.
- Object-bound share (measured by loading each package body): all 40 actions, all 55 hooks, all 11 sharing rules and both assignment rules carry an object, and so do 9 of the 10 pages. That is **117 of 206 items on an object-bound type**. The ruling's exception list does not cover them (§ "Ruling holds" below).
- Engine functions (outside the lint, open question Q1): todo 1 (`computeNextTaskDueDate`), showcase 2 (`summarizeCompletedTask`, `sweepProjectHealth`), hotcrm 0.
- Platform packages that declare `namespace: 'sys'` (service-automation, service-job, plugin-security, plugin-auth, plugin-email, plugin-sharing, plugin-approvals, platform-objects, mcp connect-ui, …): **NOT MEASURED** (their bodies are plugin registrations, not `defineStack` projects the lint loads). The ruling puts the shared `base`/`system`/`sys` namespaces outside C (#30798 phasing item 1), so they do not size the migration; slice S1 exempts them by `ManifestSchema.namespace`'s reserved list.
- Test fixtures: 281 test, testkit or fixture files call `defineStack(` with a `namespace:` somewhere, out of 434 that call it at all (`git grep -l`). This is the upper bound of the fixture sweep S1 owes. S1 measures the real red set by running the rule before it claims a file surface.
- hotcrm's five packages all declare `crm`. The prefix does not separate two modules of one artifact (two modules could both write `crm_x`). The phase-1 one-holder refusal stays the backstop for that case, and ADR-0141 co-ownership already governs it.

### 2. Stored by-name references in a live environment

A package upgrade that renames `NAME` to `NS_NAME` leaves every row below pointing at nothing. Measured by reading every platform object declaration (`*.object.ts`, 100 files) and its readers. Columns and widths are quoted from the declarations.

| # | Table · column (width) | Holds | Reader | Migration | Why |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| R1 | `sys_user_permission_set.permission_set` (100) | permission-set name | plugin-security resolution; `catalog-set-in-effect.ts` | **rewrite at upgrade** | otherwise the user silently loses the access the set gave (the card's named case) |
| R2 | `sys_user_position.position` (100) | position name | security catalog, sharing evaluator | **rewrite** | same: access silently lost |
| R3 | `sys_audience_binding_suggestion.permission_set_name` (100) | permission-set name | the suggestion confirm path | **rewrite** (pending rows) | a confirmed stale suggestion grants nothing |
| R4 | `sys_metadata_activation (metadata_type, name, package_id)` | the activation switch | `core/utils/metadata-activation-store.ts:294`, `plugin-auth` `catalog-set-in-effect.ts:42`, the automation engine's `FLOW_DISABLED` consult | **rewrite** | an empty row means "active" (ADR-0126 §4), so a lost row **silently re-arms** a flow, action or set that an admin disabled. This is the harm the object's own docblock calls a data-loss bug |
| R5 | `sys_sharing_rule.recipient_id` (200) where `recipient_type = position`, and `.name` (100) of package-managed rows | position name; rule name | plugin-sharing evaluator | **rewrite** | the evaluator matches the position by name (declaration comment, `sys-sharing-rule.object.ts` ~L203); a managed row keyed by the old rule name would sit beside the new one |
| R6 | `sys_record_share.recipient_id` (100), `sys_queue_member.recipient_id` (200) where the kind is position; `sys_queue_member.queue` (100) | position name; queue name | plugin-sharing | **rewrite** | shares and queue membership silently stop matching |
| R7 | `sys_approval_approver.approver` (255, the `position:NAME` literal); `sys_approval_request.process_name` (100, `flow:NAME`) on **open** requests | position address; source flow | plugin-approvals | **rewrite open requests**; **none** for `sys_approval_action.acted_as` on finished actions | a pending approval would wait on a slot nobody holds. A finished action is an audit fact and stays as written |
| R8 | `sys_automation_run.flow_name` (255) | flow name | `suspended-run-store.ts:656` (`status: 'paused'`), `/automation/NAME/runs` | **rewrite**: required for non-terminal runs, and done for terminal runs too | a paused or waiting run can never resume, and the run history drops out of the flow's run list |
| R9 | `sys_flow_credential.flow_name` (255) | the inbound hook secret and the http signing secret, per flow | `flow-credential-channel.ts:248` | **rewrite** | otherwise the hook stops verifying and the http node signs with nothing |
| R10 | `sys_flow_dispatch.id` (the key embeds the flow name; the docblock says it keys `(flowName, recordId, windowDay, offset)`; 30-day telemetry) | idempotency key | the dispatcher's claim, and `replay()` | **rewrite** the flow segment of keys still inside retention | otherwise one duplicate dispatch per record and window: the measured #10220 harm |
| R11 | `sys_connector_connection.connector_name` (255) | the OAuth connection of each organization | `connector-connections.ts:175/213` | **rewrite** | otherwise every organization must reconnect, and the flows fail as "not connected" until it does |
| R12 | `sys_connector_credential.connector_name`, `.package_id` | informational, comma-separated | none (keyed by `ref`, the `credentialRef`) | **none** | refreshed on the next set; the key is not a metadata name |
| R13 | `sys_assignment_cursor.rule` (100) | assignment-rule name | the round-robin assigner | **rewrite** | the round-robin silently restarts |
| R14 | `sys_job.name` / `sys_job_run.job_name` (255) | scheduled job name | `service-job` `db-job-adapter.ts` (upsert by name) | **reap the old `sys_job` row; none for runs** | a renamed job registers a new row; the stale one keeps its schedule heartbeat. Run history is history. Whether `sys_job.name` carries the `appId:jobName` key form is NOT MEASURED; S3c measures it first |
| R15 | `sys_metadata` **overlay rows** (ADR-0005) and **drafts**, keyed `(type, name, package_id)` | an environment's customization of a package item | the overlay merge, all `/meta` reads | **rewrite** (`name` plus `body.name`) | otherwise the customization silently detaches and the packaged default comes back |
| R16 | `sys_metadata` rows of a `.custom` pair (ADR-0146 D2/D9) that declare `overrides` of a base item | the base item's name | the override resolution | **rewrite the target** | otherwise the override overrides nothing |
| R17 | `sys_metadata` **bodies** of environment-authored items that name a package item: a flow node's action or subflow, an app's navigation (page, dashboard, report), a dashboard's `datasetName`, a field's `picklist`, an import's `mappingName`, a send's `template`, a skill's `tools`, a permission set's position and set references, and stored **translation** bundles keyed by item name (`flows`, `pages`, `dashboards`, `reports`, `datasets`, `positions`, `permissions`, `picklists`, `apps`, `globalActions`: `translation.zod.ts` ~L1094–1174) | references | each consumer | **rewrite at the derived reference sites** (`REFERENCE_SITES`, `reference-sites.ts`), refusing on collision as the namespace rename engine already does for objects (`package-namespace-rename.ts`) | the derived index is the one authority on "what can point at a type", so no hand-written list is added |
| R18 | free text: agent and skill `instructions`, flow `script` bodies and hook bodies that spell a name | prose and code | the AI runtime and the sandbox | **none**: they are not rewritable safely. Instead, the upgrade report lists every stored item whose text contains an old name | a rewrite inside prose or code is the guess #30794's rename engine refuses to make |
| R19 | `sys_metadata_history`, `sys_metadata_audit`, `sys_metadata_commit` | history | audit | **none** | records what was |
| R20 | `sys_email_template.name` (128) where it overlays a renamed package template | template name | the template loader | **rewrite** (zero first-party cases: hotcrm's templates already carry the namespace) | |
| R21 | `sys_api_key.scopes`, OAuth `scopes` | capability names | auth | **none** for first-party (capabilities spelled `NS.SHORT` carry the namespace by ruling 6683456244; zero capability renames measured) | a bare capability renamed by a third party is rewritten like R1 |

Not name-holding, checked and left out: `sys_personal_view.object_name` (object names do not change), `sys_user_preference.key` (free-form keys such as `plugin.ai.auto_save`; whether objectui writes item names into it is NOT MEASURED, carrier objectui), `sys_member.role` and `sys_invitation.role` (better-auth roles), `sys_scim_projection_grant.role` (the SCIM entitlement as the IdP sent it), `sys_webhook.name` (environment webhooks, not package items).

**How the rename map is derived.** It is not invented, and no new authoring key is added. The map comes from the package's own two versions: every name in version N's body that is bare and missing from version N+1, where N+1 holds `NS_NAME` of the same type in the same package. The previous body is durable in `sys_packages (id, version, manifest, metadata)` (`service-package/src/package-table.ts:111`). Whether a code-deployed artifact (hotcrm booting from its build) writes a `sys_packages` row per version is NOT MEASURED. S3 measures it first. Where no previous version is recorded, nothing is rewritten by guesswork: the boot names each dangling reference that has exactly one namespaced twin, and the operator command (S3) applies the map from a reviewed dry run. ⛔ It never rewires a dangling reference on its own. A stale assignment to a deleted set `admin` must never become a grant of a new `crm_admin`.

**Where it runs.** Open question Q4. The recommendation is inside the managed upgrade (the transaction that introduces the rename), journaled per row in `sys_migration_journal`. For code-deployed artifacts it is `os migrate bare-name-references`, recorded in `sys_migration` like every data migration (#3617), with a boot warning per dangling reference until the record verifies.

### 3. External references

| Door | Addressed by | Decision | Why |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `POST /automation/hooks/:flowName/:hookId` (inbound hook, `route-ledger.ts` ~L656) | flow name in the sender's URL | **no alias**; the upgrade report and an admin notification name every changed hook URL (Q3) | measured first-party exposure is 0: the only first-party hook flow is showcase's `intake`, already prefixed, and hotcrm has none. A permanent alias is a second spelling, which the four-axis rule refuses without named external users |
| `POST /automation/trigger/:name`, `POST /automation/:name/trigger` | flow name | **no alias**; upgrade report | the SDK callers (`automation.trigger`, `automation.execute`) are the integrator's own code |
| `POST /actions/global/:action`, `POST /actions/:object/:action[/:recordId]` | action name | **no alias**; upgrade report | the object-bound form changes too, under the ruling (§ "Ruling holds") |
| MCP `list_actions` / `run_action`, skill prompts (`prompts/get`), `agent_prompt` | names | **no alias** | MCP clients discover names through the list surfaces, which serve the new names at once |
| `GET /meta/:type/:name` (integrator reads) | item name | **no alias**; upgrade report | |
| `api` items | **`path`**, not `name` (`ApiEndpointSchema` `endpoint.zod.ts:158-159`; `endpoint-matcher.ts`) | **exclusion not needed**: renaming the item does not move the URL | |
| connector OAuth | fixed callback `GET /automation/connectors/oauth/callback` (`oauth2-grant/authorization.ts:8`), no name | **none external**; R11 covers the stored connection | |
| public forms `/forms/:slug` | `publicLink` slug (`form-routes.ts`) | **none** | views are object-derived and keep their names |
| outbound webhook payloads | whether a delivery carries the webhook name: no hit for a name header in plugin-webhooks or service-messaging | **NOT MEASURED** beyond that grep | |
| AI tool names `action_NAME` (cloud `service-ai`) | action name | **carrier: cloud** | outside this session's repositories |

Nothing breaks silently: every renamed external address is listed in the upgrade report that the rename produces. Callers get the door's existing not-found code. The alternative to the report, a `renamedTo` hint inside each door's 404 derived from the twin, adds code to six doors. I recommend against it (④), and it is listed under Q3.

### 4. Third-party packages: the lane's design call

**Call: refuse in the release that ships the rule, and ship an executable migration entry. There is no warning window and no ADR-0087 load-time conversion.**

- **Why not a load-time conversion (ADR-0087 D2):** D2 covers "losslessly mappable changes only" and excludes semantic changes. A package rename is not lossless. Bundled hook bodies and flow `script` code call names by string (`ctx.ql`). Agent and skill prose names tools. External callers hold the old URLs. And the environment's own rows (R1–R17) still hold the bare name. A conversion would rename the registry under the author without telling them, which is the silent tolerance ③ forbids. Then it would retire after one major and break later instead.
- **Why not a deprecation window:** axis ④ (过渡也从紧, 创业阶段不渐进) recommends a staged window only with named external-user evidence. Measured: no third-party package in the first-party repos. The marketplace inventory is the cloud's and was not read here.
- **What ships instead (ADR-0087 L2 + L3):**
  - `defineStack`, `os validate`, `os build`, the save door, the publish and the managed install refuse a bare name with the rename, each in its door's existing code.
  - The major's D3 migration step carries a semantic entry: bare package names become `NS_NAME`, with the lint's existing `fix` as the mechanical half and a structured TODO for free-text and code references.
  - Already-installed packages keep booting: the cold boot does not re-judge names (phase 1's posture), and the phase-1 seal still refuses a second holder.
- **The one thing the seat must ask the maintainer (Q2):** does the marketplace list any third-party package with bare names? That needs a cloud reading. If yes, a window for exactly those named packages; otherwise the call above stands.

Four axes: ① one naming rule with no per-version dialect · ② no named external pull for a window · ③ loud at authoring, with the rename in the message, rather than converted behind the author's back · ④ no conversion table to carry and retire.

### 5. Studio

- **Inside an App's design surface:** the name typed is prefixed with the pair's namespace, `NS_custom` (ADR-0146 D3; `CUSTOMIZATION_NAMESPACE_SUFFIX`, `customization-package.ts:139`). So `crm_custom_SHORT` for hotcrm, and `sys_custom_SHORT` in the platform pair. The field itself is objectui's (carrier objectui). The server's part is the save door's refusal, which names the prefixed spelling, so a client that does not prefix is still told the one right name.
- **Decision for a package-less environment item** (Setup-administered positions, permission sets and sharing rules; any write with no `packageId`): **it stays bare and is not judged.** That is today's posture for objects (`objectNamespacePrefixViolation` returns null with no package, `protocol-save-door-refusals.ts:861`). After phase 3, `NS_` names belong to packages and bare names to the environment, so the two cannot collide by construction. An environment item that bears a package item's exact name stays what ADR-0005 makes it: the overlay of that item.
- Not recommended: a new refusal of a package-less item whose name starts with an installed package's `NS_` (namespace squatting). That would be a new gate, which defaults to no without the maintainer's naming (四轴 ④). It is recorded as an acceptance note, not a question.

### 6. Length

- The namespace is at most 20 characters, the pair's included: `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,19}$` (`manifest.zod.ts` ~L565), and `MAX_CUSTOMIZATION_BASE_NAMESPACE_LENGTH = 13`, so `NS_custom` is at most 20 too. A prefixed name is therefore at most `21 + len(SHORT)`.
- The item-name pattern (`METADATA_ITEM_NAME_PATTERN`, `identifiers.zod.ts:166`) and `SnakeCaseIdentifierSchema` set no maximum. The binding limits are storage:

| Name | Binding limit | Where | Longest SHORT with a 20-character namespace |
|:--|--:|:--|--:|
| object (unchanged by phase 3; already refused at the unmanaged copy) | 63 | the table identifier: Postgres 63, MySQL 64 (`OBJECT_TABLE_IDENTIFIER_LIMIT`, `package-namespace-rename.ts:112`); SQLite, Turso and memory have no limit; Mongo's namespace limit is far above it | 42 |
| position, permission set, queue, assignment rule, sharing rule | 100 | R1, R2, R5, R6, R13 columns | 79 |
| flow | 95 | `sys_approval_request.process_name` (100) stores `flow:NAME` | 74 |
| email template | 128 | `sys_email_template.name` | 107 |
| every other type | 255 | `sys_metadata.name` (`METADATA_ITEM_NAME_STORAGE_LIMIT`) | 234 |

- The refusal sits in the same spec rule as the prefix (S1), with the per-type limit read off the declared column widths so it cannot drift. It reuses the rename engine's wording family. Message (refused at `defineStack` as `STACK_NAMESPACE_PREFIX_INVALID`, and at the save door as `NAMESPACE_PREFIX` / 422):

> Flow 'NAME' does not carry the package namespace 'NS'. Every metadata name a package authors starts with its namespace, so no two installed packages can hold the same name. Its namespaced name 'NS_NAME' is LEN characters, over the 95-character limit of the column that stores a flow's name (`sys_approval_request.process_name`, which stores `flow:NAME`). Choose a shorter name, at most 74 characters after the 'NS_' prefix, and update every reference that spells it.

- Measured headroom: the longest first-party rename is 40 characters. No first-party name comes near any limit.

### 7. The two seat-note readings

- **`tool` joins the namespaced types by construction.** `tools` is already a key of `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR` (`manifest-collection-spelling.ts:59`), so the phase-2 lint judges it today, and S1's rule, which walks the same map, refuses it with no extra code. First-party tools: 0 (hotcrm, examples). The phase-1-style backstop for packages outside C is #31414, which is open.
- **The one reader of "an agent by name" is the metadata protocol's registry read: `getMetaItem('agent', NAME)`, served as `GET /meta/agent/NAME`.**
  - That read serves package items, and the phase-1 seal guards it.
  - The kernel `metadata` service that MCP `agent_prompt` reads (`buildAgentPromptResult` → `diagnosedGet(metadataService, 'agent', …)`, `mcp-server-runtime.ts` ~L731–740) lists no package agent on a composed runtime.
  - The skill prompts already read the protocol (`listSkillPrompts` over `GET /meta/skill`, `skill-prompts.ts:122`), so agents should follow the skills.
  - ADR-0063 §2 closes `*.agent.ts` to third parties, and §4 fixes the platform ids `ask` and `build` ("no further id churn"). Those are the cloud's platform agents: built-ins, which the rule does not touch.
  - Moving `agent_prompt` onto the protocol read is not part of these slices. It widens what an MCP client is served (package agents' instructions), so it is Q5 and its own card.

### 8. The slices (PR order)

**S1 · spec rule** (`domain:spec` with the lane)
- **Files:**
  - `packages/spec/src/kernel/namespace-prefix.ts` gains the shared predicate, moved from cli per ruling 6683456244 item 2: `carriesPackageNamespace`, the platform-requested list (`guest_portal`), the not-judged collections (objects, views, docs; overrides items), the reserved namespaces (`base`, `system`, `sys`) and the per-type length table.
  - `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` `validateNamespacePrefix`: every `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR` collection.
  - `packages/cli/src/commands/lint.ts` and `utils/project-namespace.ts` import the spec predicate. The lint finding stays a warning that precedes `validate`.
  - The fixture sweep (upper bound 281 files, measured first).
  - Changeset (minor, with FROM → TO); `Skills-docs:` line, with the skills text carried by #30805.
- **Declarations:** `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` (a new exported predicate, plus a narrowed acceptance set). `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`.
